correctness.rationale: The base-four digit complement gives unique representations and exact counting CDFs. Uniform level-k Cantor approximation with error at most 2^-k and a harmonic-cost coupling prove W1=O(k2^-k). The digit inequality v^2<=3 a_v bounds every ratio by 3/2+o(1), and the unique representation gives lower 1. Lebesgue-null Cantor supports imply a full-measure gap partition and absolutely continuous inverse-square densities on each gap. Two exact families yield the density 2/t^2 on (1,3/2) with mass 2/3. Depth-L rational gap certificates miss at most 2^-L probability. Finite integer and rational tests in verify.py were executed; the infinite claims rest on the accompanying proof.

value.rationale: The normalized counting product is a central extremal statistic for additive complements, and the example is a standard sharpness witness. Its full typical-integer law is mathematically distinct from a limsup bound: a positive inverse-square density over the entire support contains exactly 2/3 of its mass, and a certified depth-L CDF has uniform error <=2^-L. The result supplies a natural exact distribution invariant and rigorous rate, not an arbitrary finite recomputation or parameter substitution.
